proposition: RentOK is the cheat code a PG owner installs once, and the month that used to knock him down — verification, collection, skips, reconciliation, complaints — becomes a level he clears in a single run.

board.style_line: Original side-scrolling platformer art, invented from scratch — chunky hand-painted game shapes with soft 16-bit-era edges, no existing game's characters, sprites, tiles or artwork; locked side-on camera, flat two-plane staging (playfield near, painted backdrop far), 9:16 vertical frame with the action band in the middle third; one implied light source, a low street sun from the upper left, hard enough to throw one short shadow per object; ground plane dull ochre concrete, backdrop graded down to smoky blue-grey, every hue desaturated except cyan #03FFF1, which is the only saturated colour in the frame:
board.negative_line: no text, no letters, no numerals, no words, no signage, no UI labels, no captions, no subtitles, no logos, no wordmarks, no watermark, no Mario, no Nintendo character or costume, no red-cap plumber likeness, no mushroom, no existing game assets or tiles, no real person's likeness, no celebrity, no gun, no muzzle flash, no blood, no gore, no Devanagari or any non-Latin glyph, no exclamation marks, no lens flare, no extra saturated hues.

identity_anchors.pg_owner: The player character: a mid-forties Indian PG owner, stocky, short-sleeved checked shirt over dark trousers, sandals, a ring of room keys clipped at his hip and a fat cloth-bound rent register tucked under his left arm with loose paper slips stuffed along its edge — an ordinary landlord of a ten-room paying-guest house, not a hero costume, no cap, no moustache gag, no uniform.
identity_anchors.rentok_mark: The supplied RentOK wordmark file (source/rentok-brand/rentok-new-logo.webp), placed by code exactly as supplied and never redrawn, restyled, regenerated, recoloured or animated in its letterforms: 'Rent' in white, 'Ok' in cyan #03FFF1, sitting on a blue #0038FF ground.
identity_anchors.ok_beam: The power-up effect: a cyan #03FFF1 aura that wraps the player like a thin outline of light, and short cyan pulses he throws forward from an open palm — light only, no weapon, no barrel, no muzzle flash; each pulse lands on an obstacle and the obstacle folds flat into a clean cyan-edged tile that slots into the ground like a paid receipt.
identity_anchors.pg_level: The level: a cross-section of one paying-guest house run as a side-scrolling street — ten identical doors along the upper storey, a stairwell, a water tank, a scooter, a notice board and a plastic chair by the gate; the same building runs left to right through every beat so the viewer is always in one continuous place.

hero_frame.description: The end-of-level flagpole. The owner stands at its base, one hand still on the pole, and behind him the whole stretch of the building he just ran through is visible in one frame: the ten doors that were dark and scuffed at the start now each carry one small cyan light, the loose paper slips that were flying out of his register in beat 1 are gone, and the fat cloth register is shut and clipped under his arm while a phone glows cyan in his other hand. The flag itself is the supplied RentOK wordmark on its blue #0038FF ground, reading clean against the dusk. Nothing is written over the picture: the frame says the mess became one glowing screen, and it says it with the doors, the shut book and the phone.

audio.music_bed: Composed on the timeline from generated stems rather than per-clip native audio, so one continuous track runs across every stitched cut. 0-9.5 s: no music at all, only the level's own sound — flat concrete footfalls, a dull wooden thud on each obstacle hit, a short sour buzzer at each knockback, and under the last-life blink a thinning pulse. 9.6 s: one clean rising arpeggio on the cheat-code reveal — the first musical note in the film, entering after the relief has already been made by picture, not before it. 10-22 s: an original eight-bar major-key loop, chiptune-adjacent but newly written, no melody quoted from any existing game, building one instrument per obstacle cleared. 22 s: it resolves onto one held chord at the flag and decays. 26.5-30 s: a single soft stamp tick under the end card, then silence. No jingle, nothing sung, no line of the message carried by audio alone.

beats.title: The jump that doesn't clear
beats.feeling: The stomach-drop a half-second before you know you are not going to make it — recognition, not comedy: this is his Tuesday.
beats.framing: Locked side-on camera, no move. The owner is small in the lower-left third zone, caught at the top of a jump, travelling left to right. The right third of the frame is filled by a squat grimy obstacle block rising past the top edge, its face scarred. Between them, three loose paper rent slips have already come out of his register and hang in the air. Backdrop: the ten doors of his own building running away behind, all dark. Foreground ground plane holds the bottom fifth. Movement: his arc peaks and begins to fall; the slips drift; nothing else moves.
beats.first_frame: Still at t_in: the owner at the exact apex of the jump, knees tucked, left arm clamping the fat register which has already slipped an inch, three white slips fanned out above and behind him mid-escape. The obstacle block's near face has just entered frame right, one third in. His shadow sits on the ground below, short, thrown from the upper-left sun. Dusk palette, nothing saturated, no cyan anywhere yet, no brand mark anywhere in the frame.
beats.impact: Camera static — the side-scroll frame is the form, and stillness here is chosen so the only motion the eye has is the escaping paper. The beat holds 2.5 s, which is the time it takes to describe the frame aloud: man, jump, block, flying paper. One dull thud on impact at 2.3 s motivates the cut out. No music. The burr image is the paper leaving the book: a PG owner recognises it instantly and it is the surprise that opens the film, not a logo and not an establishing wide.

beats.title: Two blocks, two knockbacks
beats.feeling: The small hot irritation of being sent backwards by something that should have taken a minute.
beats.framing: Same locked side-on camera, same continuous street, the camera has scrolled right by one building bay. The owner is centre-left, on the ground, mid-stagger backwards after the first block has hit him. Two obstacle blocks now stand in his path, one behind the other, both dull grey-brown with a scuffed rectangular face. Frame right, the second block's edge. His register is in both hands now, held up like a shield. Movement: his recoil left, a small dust puff at his sandals, the first block settling back into place after the hit.
beats.first_frame: Still at t_in: the owner planted on the ground, body angled back from the first block, the register raised chest-high in both hands with slips fanning out of its edge; the first block's face is a hand's width from the register's spine; the second block waits three strides behind it. One short shadow under each object, all cast the same way from upper left. Doors in the backdrop still dark, still unsaturated.
beats.impact: No camera move; the knockback is the motion. Two flat wooden thuds, 0.4 s apart, land on the two supers as code composites them — TENANT VERIFICATION on the first block's face zone, COLLECTING RENT on the second — so the words arrive on the impact, never floating free. One attention device for the beat: the recoil. Hold 2.5 s, enough to read two short supers at phone size. Sour buzzer at 4.8 s motivates the cut.

beats.title: The ones that take something with them
beats.feeling: A colder irritation than the last beat — this is the kind that costs money and cannot be argued with.
beats.framing: Same camera, scrolled one bay further right. Two new obstacles. The first is a block shaped like a room door swinging open on nothing: the room behind it is bare, mattress rolled, a padlock hanging cut. The second is a squat pile of mismatched paper — bank slips, a cash-box tray, a torn diary — heaped where a block should be, so the shape of the obstacle is literally an unreconciled heap. The owner is right of centre, arm out, reaching into the empty doorway. Movement: the door swings; one slip slides off the top of the heap.
beats.first_frame: Still at t_in: the empty room's door at the moment it reaches the end of its swing, the bare mattress visible inside, the cut padlock still rocking on its hasp; the owner's hand entering the doorway frame; the paper heap sitting in the near plane, lit by the same upper-left sun so its edges catch and its shadow falls the same way as every other object. The register is now hanging open at his side. Still no cyan, still no brand.
beats.impact: Static camera again. The door's swing is the motivating movement out of the beat. Two thuds again, same rhythm as beat 2 so the pattern is now established and the viewer can feel it repeating — that repetition is what makes the break in beat 5 land. Code composites LEFT WITHOUT PAYING on the empty doorway and NO RECONCILIATION on the heap. Hold 2.5 s: the doorway needs the extra beat to read as empty rather than merely open.

beats.title: Pinned
beats.feeling: Out of moves. Not despair — the specific fatigue of a man whose phone will not stop and who has run out of places to put things.
beats.framing: Same camera, the scroll stops for the first time in the film — the level has stopped advancing and that is the point. The owner is pushed to the left edge zone, back against the frame's left boundary, in a half-crouch. Around him, five small grey obstacle sprites are bouncing in, the swarm kind, crowding him against the edge. His register has fallen open on the ground at his feet, face down. Movement: the five sprites bounce on a tight loop; he does not advance; a thin desaturated life-bar at the top of the playfield blinks on its last segment.
beats.first_frame: Still at t_in: the owner backed against the left edge of the frame, one arm up, the register face-down and splayed at his feet with slips spilling; the five swarm sprites frozen at the tops of their bounces in a rough arc around him; the last life-bar segment lit. The backdrop is at its darkest in the film here — level follows the dramatic line. Nothing saturated. This is the lowest point and the widest the gap gets.
beats.impact: Static camera, and the withheld scroll is the device: after three beats of forward travel, the world stopping is felt before it is understood. Sound thins to the pulse under the blinking life segment — the withdrawal of the thuds is what makes the arpeggio in beat 5 audible. COMPLAINTS composites on the swarm. Held 2.0 s, the shortest beat in the film, because a held defeat turns into self-pity and the brief is not about blaming the owner: the obstacle is the absence of a system, never his competence. The cut out is motivated by the pulse hitting its last beat.

beats.title: The cheat code
beats.feeling: The exact lift of remembering there is a cheat code — the gap opened in beat 1 closing in one move.
beats.framing: Same camera, same place. One brick in the wall directly above the owner cracks and opens downward like a hit question-block, and what comes out of it is not a coin: a rectangular slab of cyan #03FFF1 light, the first saturated thing in the film, which unfolds into a floating panel carrying the supplied RentOK wordmark on its blue #0038FF ground. The owner is still low-left, now looking up, and the swarm sprites have frozen mid-bounce in the cyan wash. His phone is out of his shirt pocket and in his hand, screen up, catching the same cyan. Movement: the brick opening, the panel unfolding, the cyan light spilling down the wall and across the ground to reach him.
beats.first_frame: Still at t_in: the brick above him split along one diagonal, a hairline of cyan showing through the crack, the light not yet spilled — the whole frame is still the dusk palette with one cyan line in it. The owner's head is turned up, phone half-raised, the swarm still crowding him. The moment before the cheat code, not after it.
beats.impact: No camera move — the cyan travelling down the wall is the attention cue, and colour moves attention here as well as a push-in would, which is also why the cyan is established close and large in this beat before it has to read small in later ones. First musical note of the film enters at 9.6 s on the unfold: one rising arpeggio, channelling the relief the picture has just made rather than announcing it. This is the brand's first appearance in the film, at 9.6 s — inside ten seconds. Code composites INSTALL and RENTOK APP stacked in the upper-centre zone on the panel's own blue ground, the two lines of the cheat code. Held 3.5 s: the longest beat so far, because the panel must be read, and a beat that must be read holds its describe-aloud time.

beats.title: Power-up, and the first two go flat
beats.feeling: The specific pleasure of immunity: the thing that hurt you last time bouncing off you now.
beats.framing: Same camera, the scroll starts again and runs right. The owner is now outlined in a thin cyan aura and is upright, moving, register clipped shut under his arm and phone in his left hand. He throws a short cyan pulse forward from his open right palm. The two obstacle blocks from beat 2 are back in his path; the first pulse lands and the block folds flat into a clean cyan-edged floor tile that slots into the ground, and he runs straight over it. The swarm sprites that touch his aura bounce off and away. Movement: continuous rightward run, two pulses thrown, two blocks folding flat, the backdrop's door-lights beginning to come on one by one behind him.
beats.first_frame: Still at t_in: the owner mid-stride, first step of the run, cyan aura just closed around him, right palm open and the first pulse a compact cyan shape an arm's length ahead of it, not yet landed. The first block still standing, its face intact. Two swarm sprites already deflecting off the aura at head height. Behind him the first upper-storey door has just lit cyan; the other nine are still dark, so the payoff has somewhere to go.
beats.impact: Camera pans right with him — the first camera move in the film, motivated by an object in transit, and it is felt as release precisely because the previous five beats were locked. Music arrives underneath at full loop, one instrument added per block folded. Code composites the fixes on the tiles as they slot in: DIGITAL KYC over the first tile at 13.8 s, AUTOPAY over the second at 15.6 s, each check mark landing on the fold so word and picture agree on the same frame. Held 4.5 s: this is the action passage, so the internal cuts are quick, but each tile holds long enough to be read at phone size. Screen direction is unbroken left-to-right — the same direction he was thrown backwards against in beats 2 to 4.

beats.title: The run
beats.feeling: Momentum — the level going by faster than the problems can stand up in it.
beats.framing: Same camera, panning right, faster now. In one continuous travel the owner takes the three remaining obstacles: the empty doorway from beat 3 closes and its padlock re-seats as a pulse hits it; the paper heap collapses into a single flat cyan-edged tile; the swarm from beat 4 scatters and folds into a row of small tiles that become a stretch of clean pavement he runs across. Behind him the ten upper-storey doors light one after another in cyan. The backdrop lifts out of dusk into the brand's blue #0038FF as the run proceeds — the flood arrives through the run, not as a cut.
beats.first_frame: Still at t_in: the owner mid-run at frame centre-left, aura bright, a pulse just leaving his palm toward the empty doorway, which is still hanging open with its cut padlock; the paper heap behind it; the swarm regrouping beyond that; four of the ten doors already lit cyan behind him and six still dark; the backdrop already a shade bluer than beat 6 but not yet flooded.
beats.impact: Continuous rightward pan, no cut inside the beat until the last half-second — one shot doing what three would, so the run reads as one breath. Music adds its last three instruments on the three clears. Code composites DUES TRACKED LIVE at 17.9 s, ONE DASHBOARD at 19.4 s, COMPLAINT TICKETS at 20.7 s, each on its own tile as it slots in, each held at least 1.2 s. The performance note is that he never celebrates mid-run: he simply stops flinching, which is the honest version of the promise and keeps him the hero of the story rather than a mascot.

beats.title: The flag
beats.feeling: Earned quiet. Not triumph over anybody — the feeling of a month that finished itself.
beats.framing: The camera stops panning and settles: the end-of-level flagpole stands at the frame's right-of-centre zone, and the scene points inward to it, so centring the pole's top in the upper third is the firm statement here rather than a bull's-eye. The owner is at its base, small, one hand on the pole, shut register clipped under his arm, phone glowing cyan in his other hand. The flag is the supplied RentOK wordmark on its blue #0038FF ground, running up the pole and settling. Behind and left, the entire stretch he ran is visible in one frame: ten doors, every one carrying a small cyan light. Movement: the flag rises and settles; the doors hold; nothing else moves.
beats.first_frame: Still at t_in: the flag a third of the way up the pole, mid-rise, the wordmark already legible on its blue ground; the owner's hand closing on the pole; the register shut, clipped, with no slips showing at its edge for the first time in the film; the phone screen a clean cyan rectangle in his other hand; all ten doors lit behind him; the ground where the paper heap stood is now a run of clean cyan-edged tiles. No composited text anywhere in this beat.
beats.impact: Camera comes to rest and holds — stillness chosen, after two beats of travel, so the settling is felt. Music resolves onto one held chord as the flag reaches the top at 24.0 s, then decays across the remaining 2.5 s. This is the hero frame and it carries no copy at all: the shut book, the lit doors and the glowing phone are the whole claim, and a PG owner reads them without a word. Held 4.5 s because it is the frame the film is for, and it is the busiest frame in the film — the ten doors are the second read, kept large enough to find at phone size.

beats.title: Brand close (code-composed, nothing generated)
beats.feeling: Settled instruction. The one thing to do, with nothing else in the frame competing for it.
beats.framing: Composed entirely in code, no generative frame and no motion model: a flat blue #0038FF field filling 9:16, the supplied RentOK wordmark file placed unaltered in the upper-middle zone, the ask stacked beneath it in the centre zone, and the site line low, opposed to the mark at the other end of the long axis so the vertical frame is actually used. No illustration, no game art, no device mock-up — the last frame is the pack and nothing else.
beats.first_frame: Still: flat blue #0038FF ground; supplied wordmark unaltered, 'Rent' white, 'Ok' cyan #03FFF1; INSTALL and RENTOK APP stacked below it in white; RENTOK.COM small and low. One frame, no animation beyond a 6-frame fade up from the flag beat.
beats.impact: No camera, no model, no generated pixel: every legible string here is composed text from the text layer, which is also why nothing in the film ever asks a generative model to render a word. One soft stamp tick at 26.6 s, then silence, so the last thing the viewer hears is not a jingle. Held 3.5 s, above the time it takes to read three short lines on a phone, and the film ends on the mark.

obstacle_label_1.why: Sits on the face of the first block at the frame of impact, in the middle-third action band away from the Reels and Shorts UI furniture at top and bottom. White on the block's dull grey-brown face, measured at the darkest and lightest pixel under the letters; large weight, so 3:1 is the floor and the composite is graded to clear 4.5:1 outright. The word arrives with the thud so the label reads as the thing that hit him, not as a caption about him.

obstacle_label_2.why: Same zone, same treatment, on the second block, 1.2 s later so the two never share the frame and neither competes with the other for the one read.

obstacle_label_3.why: Placed across the empty doorway's dark interior, which is the darkest ground in the beat and therefore the highest-contrast place for white text; it also puts the words inside the emptiness they name.

obstacle_label_4.why: On the paper heap in the near plane. The heap is the busiest ground in the film, so the type sits on a graded-down patch of it and is checked against both the white slips and the dark diary underneath.

obstacle_label_5.why: Held longer than the others, 1.7 s, because it is the only label in the beat and it has to carry the lowest point alone. Centre-right zone, opposite the owner pinned at the left edge, so the word and the man sit at the two ends of the frame's width.

cheat_code.why: Stacked two lines on the cyan panel's own blue #0038FF ground in the upper-centre zone, directly under the supplied wordmark, so the mark and the instruction are one object. White on #0038FF measures well past 4.5:1. Held 2.8 s — this is the turn of the film and the only line a viewer must actually act on later, so it gets the longest single hold of any super.

fix_1.why: Lands on the cleared tile at the frame the block folds flat, answering obstacle_label_1 in the same screen position the block occupied, so the viewer feels the swap rather than being told about it. Cyan-edged tile, white type, 1.6 s.

fix_2.why: Same device, answering obstacle_label_2. Never on screen with fix_1 — one cue per moment.

fix_3.why: Answers obstacle_label_4's money problem on the tile the paper heap became. Held 1.4 s, the shortest of the fixes because it is three short words and the run is accelerating.

fix_4.why: Answers obstacle_label_4's reconciliation gap directly. Sits in the same middle band; the pan means the tile is moving under it, so the type is pinned to the tile and travels with it rather than floating in screen space.

fix_5.why: Answers obstacle_label_5, the last one standing, and clears the frame at 22.0 s so the hero frame that follows has no copy on it at all.

end_card.why: The ask, stacked under the supplied wordmark on flat #0038FF, with the site line low and opposed to the mark at the other end of the long axis so the 9:16 frame does some work instead of being tall for nothing. Three type ranks only: mark, ask, site. White on #0038FF for the ask; the site line is the smallest element in the film and is checked at delivered phone size, not at board size.

mandatory.customer_words: The video has a Mario game … An original Mario-inspired game, rather than an exact reproduction of Nintendo's character, artwork, music or game assets.
mandatory.realisation: The whole 30 s is one continuous side-scrolling platformer level, read as a game from frame one: locked side-on camera, left-to-right travel, obstacle blocks, a knockback, a life bar, a question-block, a power-up and an end-of-level flagpole. Every asset is invented for this film — an Indian PG owner in a checked shirt, not a capped plumber; a cross-section of a paying-guest house, not a mushroom kingdom; an original chiptune-adjacent score with no melody quoted. The negative_line bars Mario, Nintendo characters, existing game assets and the red-cap likeness on every prompt.

mandatory.customer_words: The player is basically a PG owner.
mandatory.realisation: The player character is the identity anchor 'pg_owner', restated verbatim in every prompt: mid-forties, checked shirt, room keys at the hip, a fat cloth rent register under his arm. He is the story's hero throughout; the brand is the guide that hands him the power, never the hero itself.
Obstacle block one in beat 2, labelled TENANT VERIFICATION on the frame of impact; cleared in beat 6 and answered on the same screen position by ✓ DIGITAL KYC.
Obstacle block two in beat 2, labelled COLLECTING RENT; cleared in beat 6 and answered by ✓ AUTOPAY.

Beat 3's first obstacle is a room door swinging open on a bare mattress with a cut padlock, labelled LEFT WITHOUT PAYING; in beat 7 a pulse closes the door and re-seats the lock, and ✓ DUES TRACKED LIVE lands on the tile.

Beat 3's second obstacle is the shape of the problem itself — a heap of bank slips, a cash-box tray and a torn diary standing where a block should be, labelled NO RECONCILIATION. In beat 7 it collapses into one flat tile under ✓ ONE DASHBOARD.

Beat 4's swarm of five small sprites that pin the owner against the left edge, labelled COMPLAINTS and held longest because it is the film's lowest point. In beat 7 the swarm folds into a row of tiles he runs across, under ✓ COMPLAINT TICKETS.

mandatory.customer_words: The game also introduces a cheat code — install RentOK app.
mandatory.realisation: Beat 5 is the cheat code and nothing else: a brick above the pinned owner cracks and unfolds a cyan panel carrying the supplied wordmark, with INSTALL / RENTOK APP composited on its blue ground and held 2.8 s — the longest single super in the film, and the brand's first appearance, at 9.6 s.

mandatory.customer_words: Mario gets a gun sort of power/immunity … Power-up design: Delegated to the creative system, while preserving the requested game-style power/immunity mechanic.
mandatory.realisation: Both halves of the mechanic are kept and the design is taken up as delegated: immunity is a thin cyan #03FFF1 aura that swarm sprites visibly bounce off (beat 6), and the ranged power is short cyan pulses thrown from an open palm that fold obstacles flat into cleared tiles (beats 6 and 7). No gun, no barrel, no muzzle flash, no violence — the effect is light, and the result is a paid receipt slotting into the ground, which keeps the mechanic while making the payoff mean something in the category.

mandatory.customer_words: It runs and kills all the obstacles
mandatory.realisation: Beats 6 and 7 are one continuous rightward run, the only camera movement in the film, in which all five labelled obstacles from beats 2 to 4 are taken in the order they were met. Each is cleared on screen; none is skipped or cut around.
Beat 8 is the flagpole, and it is the hero frame: the flag is the supplied RentOK wordmark on its blue ground, and the frame behind it shows the whole level he just cleared with all ten doors lit.
Nine contiguous beats, 0 to 30.0 s with no gap and no overlap: 2.5, 2.5, 2.5, 2.0, 3.5, 4.5, 4.5, 4.5 and a 3.5 s code-composed close carrying no generated frame (clip_s 0).

mandatory.customer_words: Platforms: Instagram Reels / Facebook and YouTube Shorts … aspect 9:16
mandatory.realisation: 9:16 throughout, with the action and every composited string kept inside the middle band so nothing collides with the platforms' own top and bottom UI furniture; the end card opposes mark and site line at the two ends of the long axis. Because these are sound-off autoplay surfaces, the film carries its whole argument on picture and composited text — see muted_test.

mandatory.customer_words: Brand and product source: Official RentOK website, https://rentok.com … identity invariants: Rent in white, Ok in cyan #03FFF1, blue #0038FF ground
mandatory.realisation: The supplied wordmark file is the only mark used, placed by code and never redrawn, recoloured or animated in its letterforms; it appears at 9.6 s on the cheat panel, at 22.0 s as the flag, and on the end card. The three invariants drive the whole palette: cyan #03FFF1 is the film's single saturated hue and the power-up's colour, and blue #0038FF is what the world floods to during the run and what the last frame is made of. RENTOK.COM closes the card as the source named in the brief.

mandatory.customer_words: Visual treatment: Delegated to the creative system.
mandatory.realisation: Taken up as a decision rather than left open: an original side-scroller in a graded-down dusk palette where cyan is the only saturated colour, so the brand hue is literally the first colour that enters the film and the world lifts into brand blue as the obstacles clear. The treatment is declared once in style_line and restated verbatim on every prompt, with four named identity anchors so the owner, the mark, the power-up and the building stay the same object across nine separately generated stills.

brand_timeline.in_context: The mark is never a sticker on the corner of the frame. At 9.6 s it is the object inside the world that changes the game — the thing the question-block gives up — and the owner looks up at it. At 22.0 s it is the flag on the pole, which is the level's own win condition, so the brand is what winning looks like rather than what is stamped on the win. At 26.5 s it is the last frame, flat and alone on its own blue ground. Across the film it is carried by three different asset types — an in-world object, an in-world flag and a composed end card — plus the colour itself, which is present from 9.5 s onward as the aura, the tiles and the flooded backdrop.
brand_timeline.spoken: none — the film has no dialogue and no voice-over, so the name is never said aloud.
